facts.notes: Surfnerd overview: 3Ms is a rocky reef break in Baja Norte and a staple of Ensenada surfing, arguably the best-known wave in the city aside from San Miguel. It serves up rippable but relatively soft lefts and rights a short paddle out, and it holds up as a fun, consistent reef. The nearby cannery and fish-processing plant do leave the water a bit dirty, and that same proximity makes things a bit sharky. Skill (surfnerd): Intermediate, Expert. Parking is the only thing worth sorting out, so ask someone nearby about the best and safest spot to leave the car. Petty theft is a known issue, so don't leave anything tempting in view. facts.name: Barra de la Cruz
facts.windOffshore: NW (surfnerd wind exposure W - N, "Offshore from NW"); NW (surfnerd guide text: "northwest (NW) offshore wind")

facts.notes: Surfnerd overview: Barra de la Cruz is a right-hand pointbreak on Mexico's Oaxacan coast, and one of the best waves in the region when it lines up. The headland's fang points southeast, cleaving south swell into dredging tubes at the top of the point that give way to steep, workable walls holding their size deep into the bay. It briefly went by the name La Jolla during the 2006 Rip Curl Pro Search event, when a rare swell served up long, world-class rights to a global webcast audience. Skill (surfnerd): Intermediate. Access (surfnerd): Getting in means a long dirt track down to the beach. Parking is paid and can be restricted, and there's a small charge for the beach facilities. Camping is available if you want to stick around for the swell.

facts.name: Barra Vieja
facts.windOffshore: NNE (surfnerd wind exposure NNW - ENE, "Offshore from NNE")
facts.notes: Surfnerd overview: Barra Vieja is a sand-bottom beachbreak sitting at the apex of a bend in the coast a few miles south of Acapulco, where the shoreline turns to face true south. This stretch of the southern Mexico Pacific coast is known for beachbreak barrels, and the ever-shifting sandbars here are kept well stocked by the Rio Papagayo, a big, muddy, debris-filled river that empties into the ocean year-round. The flat seafloor just offshore is the catch: Barra Vieja throws a lot of closeouts, and it gets uninviting when a solid south swell is pummelling the coast. Its real appeal is convenience. If you've been in Acapulco a few days and need a surf, there will almost surely be something on offer. On its day, with the right swell and the right sandbar, it can be genuinely fun. Skill (surfnerd): Beginner, Intermediate, Expert. Access (surfnerd): Access is easy.

facts.name: Beachbreak
facts.windOffshore: NE (surfnerd wind exposure N - E, "Offshore from NE"); Northeast (surf-forecast)
facts.tide: Low, Mid, High (surfnerd); Good surf at all stages of the tide. (surf-forecast)
hazards: Rips run along this stretch, so read the water before you commit. (surfnerd)
facts.season: Summer, Autumn (surfnerd); Winter, most often December (surf-forecast)
facts.notes: Surfnerd overview: Beachbreak is exactly what the name promises: a long stretch of sand that can turn on when the swell is modest, particularly when a few swells are running at once. It pulls in more size than anything around it, which cuts both ways. Once it reaches double overhead the sand can't hold the shape and it closes out. Below that, it's a fun, shifting beachbreak with both rights and lefts, and the paddle out is manageable. Skill (surfnerd): Beginner, Intermediate, Expert. Surf-forecast Beachbreak: "Beachbreak in Baja Sur is an exposed beach break that has reasonably consistent surf and can work at any time of the year. The best wind direction is from the northeast. Groundswells are more common than windswells and the best swell direction is from the southwest. The beach breaks offer lefts and rights. Good surf at all stages of the tide. Rarely crowded here. Take care of ." Access (surfnerd): This is an isolated spot, and 4WD plus camping gear is the sensible approach. Plenty of people try to drive onto the sand, and plenty of them get stuck, so think twice before following a set of tyre tracks. There's a bit of muck here and there, but the beach is mostly clean. Other guide pins from this position: surf-forecast Beachbreak 2.8 km.

Access (surfnerd): There's camping close by, and parking is free along the roadside. Other guide pins from this position: surf-forecast Cabo-Colonet 3.3 km.

facts.name: Calafia
facts.windOffshore: NNE (surfnerd wind exposure NNW - ENE, "Offshore from NNE"); N (surfnerd guide text: "north (N) offshore wind"); North-northwest (surf-forecast)
facts.tide: Mid, High (surfnerd); Best around high tide when the tide is rising. (surf-forecast)
facts.notes: Surfnerd overview: Calafia is a long right-hand point in northern Baja that breaks over an uneven reef. It is one of the first waves many visitors surf in the area, thanks to its approachable nature and its closeness to the border. Hotels, restaurants, and clubs line the cliff above the break, so it suits an easy trip south of the border more than a solo desert mission. The nearby reefs pick up swell from just about any direction, so there is usually something to surf close by. Skill (surfnerd): Intermediate. Surf-forecast Calafia_1: "Calafia in Baja Norte is an exposed point break that has fairly consistent surf. Summer offers the best conditions for surfing. Offshore winds are from the north northwest. Most of the surf here comes from groundswells and the ideal swell direction is from the south. Best around high tide when the tide is rising. Unlikely to be too crowded, even when the surf is up. Watch out for rocks." Access (surfnerd): Drive about 30 minutes south of the border, then walk down the cliff and paddle out. There is a car park with free parking, plus roadside parking if you need it. Other guide pins from this position: surf-forecast Calafia_1 1.0 km.

facts.name: Cerritos
facts.windOffshore: NE (surfnerd wind exposure N - E, "Offshore from NE"); NE (surfnerd guide text: "northeast (NE) offshore wind"); East-northeast (surf-forecast)
facts.season: Spring, Summer, Autumn, Winter (surfnerd); Winter, most often January (surf-forecast)
facts.notes: Surfnerd overview: Cerritos is a right-hand point on the Pacific side of the Baja Peninsula, about 45 minutes north of Cabo San Lucas near the village of Todos Santos. Officially it's Santa Lucia de Los Cerritos, but almost everyone just calls it Cerritos. The headland at the north end of the beach is the main event: a right that wraps around the point and gets genuinely fun and rippable once it links up with the section farther inside. It's not a hollow, world-class point, and neighboring Pedrito is arguably a touch better on its day, but the variety of waves on offer and the beach itself make Cerritos a spot worth planning around. The water is clean, and the whole stretch is being developed with condos, hotels and golf courses. Check: surfnerd states facing SW but best swell NW (90 degrees apart); both are as published. Skill (surfnerd): Beginner. Surf-forecast Cerritos: "Cerritos in Baja Sur is an exposed point break that has consistent surf and can work at any time of the year. Works best in offshore winds from the east northeast. Groundswells are more common than windswells and the best swell direction is from the west southwest. Unlikely to be too crowded, even when the surf is up." Access (surfnerd): Park right at the beach; parking is free. There are restrooms, camping and a surf school on hand, and Cerritos Beach Club and Surf has rentals and food if you turn up without gear. Other guide pins from this position: surf-forecast Cerritos 7.6 km.

facts.name: Concepción Bamba
facts.windOffshore: NW (surfnerd wind exposure W - N, "Offshore from NW"); NW (surfnerd guide text: "northwest (NW) offshore wind")
facts.notes: Surfnerd overview: Concepción Bamba is a hollow right-hander that breaks off a pair of breakwalls over boulders and sand. The main peak is a juicy, very hollow right that peels off a small breakwall for short but intense rides, while a slightly longer breakwall next door serves up a heavier, thick barreling right. Access (surfnerd): Reach the spot on a track off Highway 200 that runs beside the quarries. There's camping nearby, plus free roadside parking.

facts.name: Cuyutlan
facts.windOffshore: NNE (surfnerd wind exposure NNW - ENE, "Offshore from NNE"); NE (surfnerd guide text: "northeast (NE) offshore wind"); North-northeast (surf-forecast)
facts.notes: Surfnerd overview: Cuyutlan is a powerful beach break that breaks over sand and can throw up both lefts and rights. Most of the time it shows up as a big close-out shorebreak, but when a small, peaky southwest swell meets the straight black sandbanks it opens into tube sections for surfers quick enough to make them. There are better-shaped options along the same beach: the groynes at the Tepalcates inlet bend the swell, cut most of the wind and triangulate the sand nicely; La Termo fires off barrels in the power station outflow; and La Dos shelters the wedges beside the cliffs from north wind. Skill (surfnerd): Intermediate. Surf-forecast Cuyutlan: "Cuyutlan in Colima is an exposed beach break that only works when conditions are just right with no particular seasonal pattern. Works best in offshore winds from the north northeast. Tends to receive distant groundswells and the ideal swell angle is from the southwest. The beach break offers both left and right hand waves. It very rarely gets crowded here. Be wary of rips - they make surfing here dangerous." Other guide pins from this position: surf-forecast Cuyutlan 11.1 km.

facts.name: El Camaron
facts.swellExposure: SSE to SW, W to WNW (surfnerd)
facts.windOffshore: NNE (surfnerd wind exposure NNW - ENE, "Offshore from NNE")
facts.notes: Surfnerd overview: El Camaron is a left-hand point that peels along a rock shelf at the foot of a sea cliff, right in town. The headland juts southwest into the Pacific with no island shadow from that direction, which is what gives it a shot at swell. Most days the wave is small, soft and slow, somewhere around waist to chest high, but it still lines up and builds momentum the way a point should, and on the right board that is plenty of fun. It is fickle, and it is hardly the best wave in mainland Mexico, but when a proper swell pours in it stands up and turns highly rippable. Skill (surfnerd): Intermediate, Expert. Access (surfnerd): Park in the lot just north of the point. You will have to pay.

facts.notes: Surfnerd overview: El Paraiso is a punchy Mexican beachbreak on a ribbon of black sand between lush fields, just across the rivermouth from its more famous neighbour, Pascuales. A bend in the beach lines up triangular sandbars that throw fast, hollow, yet surprisingly forgiving waves, and while it rarely gets as perfect as Pascuales, it has no shortage of pumping days. The main wave sits right in town: a shallow, sucking beachbreak with both lefts and rights, the rights often carrying a bit more shoulder. It is a hot, humid village largely overlooked by tourists, which makes it a great place to grab a cheap meal and trade waves with the local surfers and bodyboarders. Skill (surfnerd): Intermediate. Surf-forecast El-Paraiso: "El Paraiso in Colima is an exposed beach break that has quite consistent surf and can work at any time of the year. Works best in offshore winds from the north northeast. Tends to receive distant groundswells and the best swell direction is from the southwest. The beach breaks offer lefts and rights. It very rarely gets crowded here. Watch out for rips and rocks." Access (surfnerd): There is plenty of parking once you find your way into town. Other guide pins from this position: surf-forecast El-Paraiso 1.6 km.

facts.notes: Surfnerd overview: K-38 is a bowly right-hand point just south of Rosarito, and one of the first waves many surfers ride when they start exploring Baja Norte. It breaks over a rocky reef with moderate power, and while it isn't epic, it's reliably fun and runs a decent length. That combination makes it an easy day trip from San Diego and an obvious stop on a road trip further south. The water is usually pretty clean, aside from the occasional sewage spill. Surfnerd lists this break 2 times (k-38-baja-california, k-38); merged. Second Surfnerd entry https://www.surfnerd.com/surf-forecast/k-38: workable swell S - NW (Best from S), 3ft - 12ft, Uneven Reef, Reef, Left, Right, Low, Mid, High, Intermediate. Skill (surfnerd): Intermediate, Expert. Surf-forecast K-38: "K-38 in Baja Norte is an exposed reef break that has very reliable surf and works all around the year. Offshore winds blow from the east. Groundswells more frequent than windswells and the best swell direction is from the west. Both left and right reef breaks. When it's working here, it can get crowded. Watch out for rocks." Access (surfnerd): Park at the hotel, or pay a security guard to watch your car. Petty theft is worth guarding against. facts.notes: Surfnerd overview: La Bocana is a fun sand-bottomed beachbreak and rivermouth about 30 minutes straight east of the Huatulco tourist zone. It sits very close to the road, so it is an easy check on the way past, and when it is small it is a great place to learn. The rivermouth is heavily sandbank dependent, but it is worth a look alongside the beachbreak. Huatulco is the most recent tourist destination developed by the Mexican Government, who have been keen to learn from previous mistakes. Modern water and sewage systems keep waste out of its nine pristine, if waveless, bays. Skill (surfnerd): Beginner. Access (surfnerd): There is a car park with free parking, plus roadside parking if you would rather pull up right by the sand. Facilities are on the beach.

In a land of summertime lefthanders, it is a welcome anomaly for traveling surfers. The water is usually pretty clean, though the reef is shallow enough that rocks are a real hazard. The location means that it never gets crowded. Beware of - Urchins - Rocks - Private beach - Localism." Access (surfnerd): Ask around and you will be fine, or just hike the beach. facts.notes: Surfnerd overview: La Punta is a left-hand pointbreak at the far south headland of Playa Zicatela in Puerto Escondido. The headland absorbs and refracts raw swell energy into a fun, versatile left that runs through barrel sections, ramps, steep walls and crisp shoulders. The fun shoulders out the back can turn hollow over the sandier inside sections, and the water stays a deep turquoise and bathwater warm. Check: surfnerd states facing W but best swell S (90 degrees apart); both are as published. Skill (surfnerd): Intermediate. Works best in offshore winds from the northeast. Tends to receive distant groundswells and the best swell direction is from the south southwest. The beach break provides left and right handers. It's sometimes crowded here. Beware of sharks,." Access (surfnerd): Getting there is easy: walk, drive or hop on a bus from Zicatela. There is a car park, plus camping and a surf shop close by. facts.notes: Surfnerd overview: La Saladita is a long, mirror-of-Malibu left that peels for over a minute, which is exactly how it earned the reverse nickname Ubilam. Surf-forecast La-Saladita: "La Saladita in West Guerrero is an exposed reef and point break that has consistent surf and can work at any time of the year. Offshore winds are from the northeast. Access (surfnerd): There's camping and a surf school in the area, plus free parking. Reaching the wave means a long paddle out to the point, and the spot sits about 45 minutes' drive from Zihuatanejo, with decent accommodation and surf camps nearby. facts.notes: Surfnerd overview: Las Islitas is the right-hand point that carries the Guinness Book of Records certification for the longest wave in the world, a 5,700ft (2250m) ride that wraps all the way into Matanchen Bay. On its day it's a mellow wall with occasional tubing sections, and if your legs still work at the end, you've got a long walk back to the point ahead of you. The catch is that new construction has changed the setup, and it now hardly ever breaks. It struggles to repeat the form that made it a destination in the '60s and '70s, and that record-breaking ride was almost certainly measured on the best day the place has ever seen. Check: surfnerd states facing ESE but best swell S (67.5 degrees apart); both are as published. Surf-forecast Las-Islitas: "Las Islitas (Matanchen Bay) in Nayarit is a quite exposed point/jetties break. Summer offers the best conditions for surfing. Ideal winds are from the north northeast. Tends to receive distant groundswells and the best swell direction is from the south. Rarely crowded here. Hazards include rips, sharks and rocks." Access (surfnerd): Free roadside parking. facts.notes: Surfnerd overview: Los Corchos is a sand-bottom beachbreak with peaks that break both left and right. Don't expect the punch of Puerto Escondido, Mexico's benchmark beachbreak, because the banks here have no power and the peaks usually run soft. When river flow lines up the sandbars the peaks can take on good shape, but more often the waves turn junky and get blown out. After rain, the water can also get polluted. Skill (surfnerd): Beginner. Surf-forecast Playa-Los-Corchos: "Playa Los Corchos in Nayarit is an exposed beach break that only works when conditions are just right with no particular seasonal pattern. Offshore winds blow from the northeast. Most of the surf here comes from groundswells and the best swell direction is from the west. The beach break offers both left and right hand waves. Rarely crowded here. Watch out for rips, sharks and rocks." Access (surfnerd): There's a car park with free parking. Other guide pins from this position: surf-forecast Playa-Los-Corchos 1.7 km.

facts.notes: Surfnerd overview: Los Pinos is a fun, shifty left point on the northern coast of Mazatlan's cape, in El Centro. Summer swell wraps in and organizes into zipping lefthand lines that first break over a shallow rock reef before spilling into a tiny bay rimmed by a wide, pink-sand beach. The lefts hold enough face to crack the lip and work up some speed, and it stands out as one of Mazatlan's more consistent waves. When it gets really big it does tend to soften out, though the lineup thins out along with it. Skill (surfnerd): Intermediate, Expert. Surf-forecast Los-Pinos: "Los Pinos in Sinaloa is a fairly exposed point break that has pretty consitent surf. Summer offers the best conditions for surfing. Offshore winds are from the east. Most of the surf here comes from groundswells and the best swell direction is from the southwest.There is a left breaking point here. Best around mid tide when the tide is falling. Relatively few surfers here, even on good days. Take care to avoid the rocks." Access (surfnerd): Park off Paseo Claussen. Other guide pins from this position: surf-forecast Los-Pinos 7.8 km.

facts.name: Manzanillo - Colima

facts.notes: Surfnerd overview: Manzanillo is a big bay on the Colima coast with sand-bottomed beach breaks peeling both left and right. Most surfers arriving in the area start here, and the bay holds a few very different setups: Playa Miramar is the gentle end of things for learners on a small south swell, Olas Altas turns challenging for the local crew when southwest to west pulses arrive, and La Boquita offers a super protected right point on huge days. Skill (surfnerd): Beginner. Access (surfnerd): There is a surf school in the area if you want a hand getting started. Parking is easy enough, with a free car park plus roadside spots.

Best around mid tide. A popular wave that can get growded. Take care of rips and rocks." Access (surfnerd): Park above the break, right by Misiones del Cabo. facts.notes: Surfnerd overview: Morro Ayuta Point is an excellent right-hand sand pointbreak, marked by an out-of-service lighthouse and almost impossible to find without local knowledge or a surf guide. Barreling waves peel off the top of the headland, and the rides get very long when everything lines up. Beachbreak peaks also break out in the bay, a turtle nesting haven backed by a small fishing community. Check: surfnerd states facing E but best swell S (90 degrees apart); both are as published. Skill (surfnerd): Intermediate. Access (surfnerd): There is camping nearby if you want to stick around for a swell.

facts.name: Nine Palms
facts.windOffshore: WNW (surfnerd wind exposure WSW - NNW, "Offshore from WNW"); NW (surfnerd guide text: "northwest (NW) offshore wind"); Northwest (surf-forecast)
facts.exposure: exposed (surf-forecast: "fairly exposed reef and point break")
hazards: urchins, rips, rocks, locals and pollution (surf-forecast)
Watch out for rocks, and after a good one, expect a paddle back out. (surfnerd)
facts.season: Spring, Summer, Autumn (surfnerd); Summer, most often July (surf-forecast)
facts.notes: Surfnerd overview: Nine Palms is a right-hand point on Baja Sur's East Cape, breaking over uneven reef with sand and rock underneath. It has been a fixture on Cabo surf itineraries for decades, and while it isn't world-class, it's one of the most popular waves on this stretch of coast. The point is well sheltered from the wind and lines up nicely on a big south swell. Expect fun, fast-crumbling walls rather than tubes, though impeccable timing can turn up a sneaky barrel. Check: surfnerd states facing ESE but best swell S (67.5 degrees apart); both are as published. Skill (surfnerd): Beginner. Surf-forecast Nine-Palms: "Nine Palms in Baja Sur is a fairly exposed reef and point break that has consistent surf. Summer offers the optimum conditions for surfing. Offshore winds blow from the northwest. Most of the surf here comes from groundswells and the ideal swell direction is from the south. A right hand reef. Even when there are waves, it's not likley to be crowded. Beware of urchins, rips, rocks, locals and pollution." Access (surfnerd): Park right above the break for free. There's camping at the spot. Other guide pins from this position: surf-forecast Nine-Palms 7.9 km.

Check: surfnerd states facing E but best swell S (90 degrees apart); both are as published. Skill (surfnerd): Expert. Surf-forecast Open-Doors: "Open Doors (Isla Natividad) in Baja Sur is an exposed beach break that has pretty consitent surf. Summer offers the optimum conditions for surfing. Ideal winds are from the northwest. Tends to receive distant groundswells and the best swell direction is from the southwest. The beach break favours left handers. Even when there are waves, it's not likley to be crowded. Take care of rips, sharks and rocks." Access (surfnerd): There is camping nearby, though parking is restricted, so plan your approach before you arrive. Other guide pins from this position: surf-forecast Open-Doors 1.0 km.

facts.name: Pascuales
facts.windOffshore: NE (surfnerd wind exposure N - E, "Offshore from NE"); NE (surfnerd guide text: "northeast (NE) offshore wind"); North-northeast (surf-forecast)
hazards: This is an expert wave through and through: when it's pumping, the current is treacherous and the poundings are as brutal as they get, so if you're not fully comfortable in serious surf it won't be your cup of tea. (surfnerd)
facts.season: Spring, Summer, Autumn (surfnerd); Winter, most often December (surf-forecast)
facts.notes: Surfnerd overview: Pascuales is a heavy black-sand beachbreak on the Colima coast, Mexico's answer to Oaxaca's famous Puerto Escondido. It throws thick, fast, powerful barrels and terrifying, mutant A-frames with enough force to snap a gun and dent the biggest ego. Pound for pound it's every bit as heavy as Puerto, breaking both left and right over sand. This is an expert wave through and through: when it's pumping, the current is treacherous and the poundings are as brutal as they get, so if you're not fully comfortable in serious surf it won't be your cup of tea. Skill (surfnerd): Expert. Surf-forecast Pascuales: "Pascuales in Colima is an exposed river break that only works when conditions are just right with no particular seasonal pattern. The best wind direction is from the north northeast. Tends to receive distant groundswells and the best swell direction is from the southwest. Waves at the river break both left and right. Rarely crowded here. Watch out for sharks." Access (surfnerd): There's parking right on the beach and camping on hand. Keep an eye on your gear, though, as thieves are a problem at the campsite. Other guide pins from this position: surf-forecast Pascuales 0.3 km.

facts.name: Patoles
facts.windOffshore: E (surfnerd wind exposure NE - SE, "Offshore from E")
facts.notes: Surfnerd overview: Patoles is a long left-hander that peels off a point where the Pacific meets the Gulf of California. A 90-degree elbow in the coast sits at just the right angle to wrap south swell into fast, zippy walls, and the bottom is a mix of sand and rock. Most of the time it lands somewhere in the ridiculously fun range, but the bigger swells can turn it into a proper pumping wave with real barrels. It sits close to town. Skill (surfnerd): Intermediate, Expert. Access (surfnerd): Getting in is difficult during and after heavy rains.

facts.notes: Surfnerd overview: Petacalco is a powerful right-hander on the Mexican coast, breaking over sand. Its long, intense righthand barrels were once counted among the best surf on the planet, but expansion of the neighbouring port of Lázaro Cárdenas turned the wave into an ugly closeout. It has since risen from the ashes and is rideable again. Pollution is part of the picture here, drifting in from the rivermouth, the port, and nearby factories. Skill (surfnerd): Expert. Surf-forecast Petacalco: "Petacalco in West Guerrero is an exposed point/sandbar break that only works when conditions are just right. Summer offers the favoured conditions for surfing. Ideal winds are from the north northwest. Groundswells more frequent than windswells and the ideal swell direction is from the south southwest. It's sometimes crowded here. Watch out for rips, sharks,stingrays." Other guide pins from this position: surf-forecast Petacalco 4.7 km.

facts.name: Playa Azul
facts.windOffshore: NNE (surfnerd wind exposure NNW - ENE, "Offshore from NNE"); North-northeast (surf-forecast)
facts.tide: Low, Mid (surfnerd); The quality of the surf isn't affected by the tide. (surf-forecast)
hazards: Because the surfing landscape is so wide, plan on drifting a long way from your paddle-out spot, and on some bicep-burning current on the paddles back out. (surfnerd)
Strong currents and long paddles are part of the deal here, and turning your back to the ocean is the main way to get caught out. (surfnerd)
facts.season: Spring, Summer, Autumn (surfnerd); Summer, most often July (surf-forecast)
facts.notes: Surfnerd overview: Playa Azul is a vast, grab-bag beachbreak where peaks bulge up and down the sand and you can more or less paddle straight out from wherever you park. Anyone who has surfed Baja Malibu in Northern Baja will spot the family resemblance immediately: glassy mornings, fast walls, and round barrels. It is an often-overlooked jewel, and the water is clean. Skill (surfnerd): Intermediate, Expert. Surf-forecast Playa-Azul: "Playa Azul in Michoacan is a quite exposed beach break that has very consistent surf. Summer offers the best conditions for surfing. Offshore winds blow from the north northeast. Most of the surf here comes from groundswells and the ideal swell angle is from the southwest. The beach breaks offer lefts and rights. The quality of the surf isn't affected by the tide. When it's working here, it can get crowded. Beware of rips and sharks." Access (surfnerd): Park at any of the restaurants along the beach and walk straight down to the sand. Other guide pins from this position: surf-forecast Playa-Azul 14.5 km.

Take care of rips and rocks." Access (surfnerd): Drive down to the beach, walk across the rocks, and paddle out through a mellow, easy channel. There's free roadside parking, plus camping, a surf school, and a surf shop nearby. Other guide pins from this position: surf-forecast Playa-Linda_1 1.8 km.

facts.name: Puerto Escondido
facts.windOffshore: NE (surfnerd wind exposure N - E, "Offshore from NE"); NE (surfnerd guide text: "northeast (NE) offshore wind"); North-northeast (surf-forecast)
hazards: Stay switched on in the water: strong currents, powerful rips, and heavy, board-snapping waves are all part of the deal, and it's worth keeping an eye on your gear for theft. (surfnerd)
facts.season: Spring, Summer, Autumn (surfnerd); Winter, most often November (surf-forecast)
facts.notes: Surfnerd overview: Puerto Escondido is a world-class beachbreak on Zicatela Beach, widely known as the "Mexican Pipeline." Powerful, cavernous barrels unload close to shore over a sand bottom, throwing up both lefts and rights. A deep offshore trench focuses and amplifies incoming swell, which is why the waves jack up so dramatically. It earns its excellent rating, but once it gets overhead this is committed, expert territory only. Skill (surfnerd): Expert. Surf-forecast Puerto-Escondido: "Puerto Escondido in Oaxaca is an exposed beach and point break that has very reliable surf. Summer offers the favoured conditions for surfing. Offshore winds blow from the north northeast. Tends to receive distant groundswells and the best swell direction is from the south southwest. Waves at the beach break both left and right Sometimes crowded. Watch out for rips and sharks." Access (surfnerd): Getting to the beach is straightforward, with restrooms, showers, a surf school, and a surf shop on hand, plus lifeguards watching the water. Parking is easy, with a car park offering free parking alongside paid and roadside options. Stay switched on in the water: strong currents, powerful rips, and heavy, board-snapping waves are all part of the deal, and it's worth keeping an eye on your gear for theft. Other guide pins from this position: surf-forecast Puerto-Escondido 2.2 km.

facts.notes: Surfnerd overview: Punta Burros is a fun, semi-soft right-hand reef about 40 minutes' drive from Puerto Vallarta, with a lower-quality left on offer too. The wave breaks over rock and coral, and the water stays relatively clean. It is forgiving enough to suit beginners, though the crowd is the real filter here. Paddling out takes a bit of work without being taxing. Skill (surfnerd): Beginner, Intermediate, Expert. Surf-forecast Punta-Burros: "Punta Burros in Nayarit is a fairly exposed reef break that has reliable surf. Winter is the favoured time of year for surfing here. The best wind direction is from the north northeast. Groundswells more frequent than windswells and the optimum swell angle is from the west northwest. There is a right hand reef break. When it's working here, it can get crowded. Beware of urchins, rocks and locals." Access (surfnerd): Three ways in. Park at (or stay at) Palladium Vallarta Resort and walk 10 minutes to the wave. Park on the road to the resort and walk 20 minutes. Or hire a panga in El Enclote or one of the nearby small fishing villages. Other guide pins from this position: surf-forecast Punta-Burros 0.9 km.

facts.name: Punta Chivo
facts.windOffshore: WNW (surfnerd wind exposure WSW - NNW, "Offshore from WNW"); W (surfnerd guide text: "west (W) offshore wind")
hazards: Watch out for gap winds and mid-day sunburn. (surfnerd)
facts.notes: Surfnerd overview: Punta Chivo is a right-hand sand-bottom point near Salina Cruz, and it's the one nearly every traveling surfer here ends up surfing at least once. It's the blue-collar cousin of the more famous, more photographed points in the region: less glamorous, but dependable. The wave is a fun, tapered wall running off a large sentinel rock, with racy sections and the occasional hollow bit that can turn into a genuinely good tube when the sand lines up. Getting there means passing through a small fishing village and walking out to the point. Check: surfnerd states facing ESE but best swell S (67.5 degrees apart); both are as published. Skill (surfnerd): Beginner. Access (surfnerd): Access is straightforward by 4x4, then a walk out to the point through the fishing village. There's free parking as well as roadside parking. Salina Cruz has up to 15 breaks with options for all skill levels, and a handful of surf camps and surf schools are based around them.

facts.windOffshore: WNW (surfnerd wind exposure WSW - NNW, "Offshore from WNW"); W (surfnerd guide text: "west (W) offshore wind"); North (surf-forecast)
facts.season: Summer, Autumn, Spring (surfnerd); Summer, most often July (surf-forecast)
facts.notes: Surfnerd overview: Punta Conejo is the premier right-hand pointbreak just west of Salina Cruz, a sand-bottom point known for machine-like, impossibly long walls. On the right day it delivers rides up to 500 meters, with ten-turn walls standard and the occasional dredging tube on the inside when the sandbanks line up. It is widely considered one of the most fun and user-friendly right points anywhere, and it suits the average regular-footer especially well. Check: surfnerd states facing ESE but best swell S (67.5 degrees apart); both are as published. Skill (surfnerd): Intermediate, Expert. Surf-forecast Punta-Conejo_1: "Punta Conejo in Oaxaca is an exposed point break that has reasonably consistent surf. Summer offers the best conditions for surfing. Works best in offshore winds from the north. Groundswells more frequent than windswells and the ideal swell direction is from the south southwest. Rarely crowded here. Beware of sharks and rocks." Access (surfnerd): Getting in is straightforward by 4x4, but as with all spots around Salina Cruz you'll need a local guide. There's camping nearby, along with free roadside parking. Other guide pins from this position: surf-forecast Punta-Conejo_1 5.2 km.

facts.notes: Surfnerd overview: Punta San Carlos is a long, mellow right-hand point on the remote Pacific side of Baja, breaking over rock and reef. It's a forgiving wave that rewards a patient approach, and it marks the northern end of a stretch of right point after right point running south toward Punta Rosarito and the Seven Sisters. The water here is clean, and the point has also become a well-known kiteboarding and windsurfing destination thanks to the strong northwesterlies that funnel down the coast. Skill (surfnerd): Beginner, Intermediate, Expert. Surf-forecast Punta-San-Carlos: "Punta San Carlos in Baja Norte is an exposed reef and point break that has reasonably consistent surf. Summer offers the optimum conditions for surfing. Offshore winds blow from the northeast. Most of the surf here comes from groundswells and the ideal swell angle is from the southwest. The right hand reef break is better than the left. It very rarely gets crowded here. Hazards include urchins and rocks." Access (surfnerd): Getting here is difficult. This stretch of the Pacific coast sits a long way from the highway, so plan on carrying in everything you need, including all your water and gas. The paddle out itself is light once you're there. Other guide pins from this position: surf-forecast Punta-San-Carlos 3.0 km.

facts.notes: Surfnerd overview: Punta Sayulita is the reef setup wrapping around the headland at the north end of Sayulita, where a broad sandy beach faces slightly north of west and the point itself swings to true north. The main attraction is the righthander in the middle of town, a shifty wave that runs as a mellow longboard ride most days and picks up a higher-performance edge on a solid swell. A cleaner lefthander breaks off the beach on the north end of town, peeling in sectiony lines that longboarders will enjoy and shortboarders can find worthwhile when the swell lines up. The waves break over an uneven reef of sand and rock, and the whole setup stays forgiving enough to suit beginners and longboarders. Check: surfnerd states facing NNW but best swell W (67.5 degrees apart); both are as published. Skill (surfnerd): Beginner. Surf-forecast Punta-Sayulita: "Punta Sayulita in Nayarit is an exposed beach and reef break that is usually a safe bet. Summer offers the best conditions for surfing. The best wind direction is from the east. Tends to receive distant groundswells and the best swell direction is from the west southwest. A left hand reef break. It's sometimes crowded here. Submerged rocks are a hazard." Access (surfnerd): There is plenty of parking, both free and roadside. You will find camping, a surf school, and a surf shop nearby, and it is a good base for hiring a boat out to the Punta Mita breaks. Other guide pins from this position: surf-forecast Punta-Sayulita 1.4 km.

Even when there are waves, it's not likley to be crowded. Watch out for rocks." Beware of rips and rocks." Access (surfnerd): Getting to the beach can be tricky thanks to the exclusive resorts stretching across it. Once you're there you'll find restrooms, showers, a lifeguard, and camping, plus a car park with free parking and roadside spots. facts.notes: Surfnerd overview: Rio Nexpa is a long, occasionally barreling left that peels down the cobblestone fan of a wide rivermouth in southern Michoacan, and it ranks among Mexico's best lefts when a solid south swell is running. Good surf at all stages of the tide. Often Crowded. Beware of rips and rocks." Access (surfnerd): Once you find the turn-off from the highway, access is easy. facts.name: Rosarito Beach
facts.swellExposure: SSE to WNW, WNW to NNW (surfnerd)
facts.windOffshore: ENE (surfnerd wind exposure NNE - ESE, "Offshore from ENE"); East (surf-forecast)
facts.tide: Mid (Best at Mid, Better on rising) (surfnerd)
facts.season: Spring, Summer, Autumn, Winter (surfnerd); Summer, most often July (surf-forecast)
facts.notes: Surfnerd overview: Rosarito Beach is a long ribbon of sand fronting the hotels of a town that spent generations as Northern Baja's party capital. The whistles and dance floors went quiet when the cartel wars arrived in 2007, and tourism is only slowly returning. The waves never stopped, but honestly, Rosarito was never much of a surfing hotspot given how many high-grade options Northern Baja has. The beach here is flat and faces directly west, so it's a town break worth a paddle if you're already around, not a destination. Head out of town for the pumping points and beachbreaks nearby. Sandbars do most of the work. A couple of rivers spill into the surf and throw up good, if fleeting, banks, and the pier in front of the Rosarito Beach Hotel builds decent sand of its own. Both rights and lefts turn up depending on the bank. Skill (surfnerd): Beginner, Intermediate, Expert. Surf-forecast Rosarito: "Rosarito in Baja Norte is an exposed beach,reef and rivermouth break that has dependable surf. Summer offers the optimum conditions for surfing. The best wind direction is from the east. Waves just as likely from local windswells as from distant groundswells and the best swell direction is from the southwest. The beach break provides left and right handers and there are also left and right hand reef breaks on offer.. Be aware that the sea here is polluted." Access (surfnerd): Numerous parking areas sit right on the sand. Lock your car and hide anything valuable, since petty theft is a common occurrence, and be aware that corrupt police officers are part of the picture too. Other guide pins from this position: surf-forecast Rosarito 1.7 km.

facts.notes: Surfnerd overview: Salina Cruz is a stretch of right-hand pointbreaks that grind along for a mind-bendingly, leg-crampingly long time. Pick up one that has already been spinning for tens of yards and you'll still get a lengthy ride out of it, through barrel sections, crisp lips, pocket shoulders and every other manner of blissful kink. The waves break over sand with scattered rock, the water is clean, and the surf here is really good. Some of the spots can get shallow, so keep an eye on what's under you. After a ride that long, expect an equally long paddle back out. Skill (surfnerd): Intermediate, Expert. Surf-forecast Salina-Cruz: "Salina Cruz in Oaxaca is an exposed beach break that has quite consistent surf. Summer offers the best conditions for surfing. Offshore winds are from the north. Tends to receive distant groundswells and the best swell direction is from the south southwest. The beach break provides left and right handers. It very rarely gets crowded here. Watch out for sharks ,rocks and pollution." Access (surfnerd): Getting there is a bit tricky. Other guide pins from this position: surf-forecast Salina-Cruz 14.2 km.

facts.name: Salsipuedes
facts.windOffshore: NNE (surfnerd wind exposure NNW - ENE, "Offshore from NNE"); NE (surfnerd guide text: "northeast (NE) offshore wind"); North-northeast (surf-forecast)
facts.tide: Low (Best at Low, Better on rising) (surfnerd)
facts.season: Autumn, Winter (surfnerd); Summer, most often September (surf-forecast)
facts.notes: Surfnerd overview: Salsipuedes is a right-hand pointbreak in Northern Baja, and arguably the best in the region. It's really two waves in one spot. Up toward the top of the point sits a reef A-frame that throws bowly lefts and longer, sectiony rights. Around the bend to the south is the main event: a thick, hollow righthander that on its rare best days ranks among the heaviest, meanest points on the North American West Coast. Those world-class moments don't come often, so the reef is the more dependable source of fun. Check: surfnerd states facing SSW but best swell NW (112.5 degrees apart); both are as published. Skill (surfnerd): Expert. Surf-forecast Salsipuedes: "Salsipuedes in Baja Norte is an exposed reef and point break that has fairly consistent surf. Summer offers the best conditions for surfing.. Groundswells are more common than windswells and the ideal swell direction is from the southwest. Both left and right reef breaks. Even when there are waves, it's not likley to be crowded. Watch out for rocks." Access (surfnerd): Getting here is the hard part. Public road access is gone, so a boat is the best and realistically the only way in, and parking is restricted. Watch for shallow rock sections, and factor in the real risk of a long boat trip that ends with nothing to surf. Other guide pins from this position: surf-forecast Salsipuedes 4.0 km.

facts.windOffshore: N (surfnerd wind exposure NW - NE, "Offshore from N")
facts.notes: Surfnerd overview: San Agustin is a sand-bottom beachbreak on Mexico's southern Pacific coast, tucked into a broad, exposed white-sand bay on the western flank of Parque Nacional Huatulco. The bay sits at the heart of Mexico's push toward environmentally sound, sustainable tourism, and the water is relatively clean. A scattering of peaks gives you rights and lefts to pick from, and of the few bays chewed into this raw stretch of coastline, San Agustin is one of the better options. Skill (surfnerd): Beginner, Intermediate, Expert. Access (surfnerd): San Agustin is close to the Huatulco airport, close enough that you can cross the street and head for the coast, but the last stretch is a handful of bumpy track miles and getting down there is the hard part.

facts.notes: Surfnerd overview: San Antonio del Mar is a stretch of sand-bottom beachbreaks with shifting banks that peel both left and right. The setting is remote: cliffs rise to the south toward Cabo Colonet and steadily cut off beach access, while a scattering of right points waits to the north at Punta San Jose and around Cabras. Because the banks take all swells and directions, there's potential for quality surf right through the year. Check: surfnerd states facing W but best swell S (90 degrees apart); both are as published. Skill (surfnerd): Intermediate. Surf-forecast San-Antonio-Del-Mar: "San Antonio Del Mar in Baja Norte is an exposed beach break that has pretty consitent surf. Autumn and winter are the favoured times of year for waves. The best wind direction is from the east northeast. Tends to receive distant groundswells and the optimum swell angle is from the west northwest. The beach break provides left and right handers. Rarely crowded here. Watch out for rocks." Access (surfnerd): Free-camping is the way to post up here, with free parking available along the roadside. Bear in mind that the cliffs to the south steadily reduce beach access the further you head toward Cabo Colonet. Other guide pins from this position: surf-forecast San-Antonio-Del-Mar 0.9 km.

facts.notes: Surfnerd overview: San Blas sits about 80 miles north of Vallarta, where the coastline starts jutting back out into the Pacific far enough to catch south swell pulses through spring and summer. The town marks the beginning of that fortunate geological shift, and it is mostly beachbreak heaven in and around it, with waves peeling both right and left over sand. Two points break up the run of banks: Stoner's Point just south of town, a mellow cobblestone righthander, and Santa Cruz on the other side of the bay, a lefthand point. On its day it is a decent beachbreak, and quality depends a lot on the swell that shows up. The water is usually pretty clean, though it can turn after a big rain. Skill (surfnerd): Beginner, Intermediate, Expert. Surf-forecast San-Blas: "San Blas in Nayarit is an exposed beach and reef break that has unreliable waves. Summer offers the best conditions for surfing. Offshore winds blow from the northeast. Tends to receive distant groundswells and the ideal swell angle is from the southwest. Waves at the beach break both left and right. Surfable at all stages of the tide. It's sometimes crowded here. Beware of rocks, rips." Access (surfnerd): Getting in is easy. facts.name: San Juan de Alima
facts.windOffshore: NE (surfnerd wind exposure N - E, "Offshore from NE"); NE (surfnerd guide text: "northeast (NE) offshore wind"); Northeast (surf-forecast)
facts.exposure: exposed (surf-forecast: "fairly exposed beach and point break")
facts.notes: Surfnerd overview: San Juan de Alima sits just over the state border into Michoacan, where a beach break peels both left and right over sand. The standout is Punta la Playa, a long right point sheltered from the afternoon seabreezes, and when the point isn't firing there are plenty of beachbreaks out in front of town to fall back on. A little to the southeast you'll find three reefs with easy channels and the fun peaks at Las Brisas. Check: surfnerd states facing SW but best swell NW (90 degrees apart); both are as published. Skill (surfnerd): Beginner. Surf-forecast San-Juande-Alima: "San Juan de Alima in Michoacan is a fairly exposed beach and point break that has fairly consistent surf. Winter is the best time of year for surfing here. The best wind direction is from the northeast. Tends to receive distant groundswells and the ideal swell direction is from the northwest. The beach break offers both left and right hand waves Even when there are waves, it's not likley to be crowded. Be wary of rips - they make surfing here dangerous." Access (surfnerd): There's camping close by and a surf school on hand if you want help getting started. Other guide pins from this position: surf-forecast San-Juande-Alima 2.1 km.

facts.name: San Miguel - Baja
facts.swellExposure: S to SSW, SW to W (surfnerd)
facts.windOffshore: N (surfnerd wind exposure NW - NE, "Offshore from N"); NE (surfnerd guide text: "northeast (NE) offshore wind"); East (surf-forecast)
hazards: The bottom is rocky with some urchins, so mind your feet, and give the local crew their space in a crowded peak. (surfnerd)
facts.season: Autumn, Winter (surfnerd); Winter, most often January (surf-forecast)
facts.notes: Surfnerd overview: San Miguel is a long, tapered right-hand point that peels over cobblestones and boulders in Northern Baja. The takeoff is steep and fast, and the wall stretches out down the line, growing and contracting as it reels along and leaving room for both lip work and the occasional barrel. It earns its reputation as one of the standout waves in the area. Check: surfnerd states facing S but best swell NW (135 degrees apart); both are as published. Skill (surfnerd): Expert. Surf-forecast San-Miguel: "San Miguel in Baja Norte is a fairly exposed point break that has reliable surf. Autumn and winter are the best times of year for waves. Works best in offshore winds from the east. Tends to receive distant groundswells and the best swell direction is from the west northwest. A popular wave that can get growded. Hazards include urchins, rocks, locals and pollution." Access (surfnerd): Park at the point, where you'll find a car park with free, paid, and roadside options. Camping is available on site if you want to stay for the swell. Other guide pins from this position: surf-forecast San-Miguel 1.7 km.

facts.windOffshore: ESE (surfnerd wind exposure ENE - SSE, "Offshore from ESE"); E (surfnerd guide text: "east (E) offshore wind"); East (surf-forecast)

facts.notes: Surfnerd overview: San Pancho is a fast left-hand point break near the large Costa Azul resort. You're not in California, but after Santa Cruz comes San Francisco, or San Pancho as the locals call it. It breaks over a mix of uneven reef and sand, with a quick lefthander peeling off the point and a sucky peak in front of the river that can hold some size and gets hollow around low tide. Check: surfnerd states facing WNW but best swell SW (67.5 degrees apart); both are as published. Skill (surfnerd): Intermediate. Surf-forecast San-Pancho: "San Pancho(San Francisco) in Nayarit is an exposed reef break that has fairly consistent surf. Summer offers the best conditions for surfing. Ideal winds are from the east. Groundswells are more common than windswells and the optimum swell angle is from the west southwest. There is a left hand reef break. Sometimes crowded. Take care of rips, sharks and rocks." Access (surfnerd): There's camping and a surf shop close by. Other guide pins from this position: surf-forecast San-Pancho 1.6 km.

facts.name: San Pedrito
facts.windOffshore: NE (surfnerd wind exposure N - E, "Offshore from NE"); Northeast (surf-forecast)
facts.tide: Mid (Best at Mid, Better on rising) (surfnerd); Surfable at all stages of the tide. (surf-forecast)
hazards: Sharp rocks are the main hazard, and some surfers wear booties because of it. (surfnerd)
facts.season: Spring, Summer, Autumn, Winter (surfnerd); Winter, most often January (surf-forecast)
facts.notes: Surfnerd overview: San Pedrito is a rock reef just outside the dusty village of Todos Santos, on the last stretch of the peninsula's west coast before you hit the glitz of Cabo San Lucas. Don't confuse this Todos Santos with the little island up north that holds the big wave called Killers. This one keeps three seriously fun waves in its quaint jurisdiction: Los Cerritos, La Pastora and San Pedrito. Being about 45 minutes north of Cabo on the west coast changes things. The water can run five to eight degrees Fahrenheit colder, the winds blow harder, and the days turn foggier. The trade-off is worth it, because the surf here is always bigger, often a whole lot bigger. It's an extremely fun wave, and the main attraction is the righthander, though the reef throws up lefts too. Skill (surfnerd): Intermediate, Expert. Surf-forecast San-Pedrito_Todos-Santos: "San Pedrito(Todos Santos) in Baja Sur is an exposed beach break that has reasonably consistent surf and can work at any time of the year. Works best in offshore winds from the northeast. Tends to receive distant groundswells and the ideal swell direction is from the west southwest. The beach break provides left and right handers. Surfable at all stages of the tide. It's often crowded here. Watch out for urchins, rips and rocks." Access (surfnerd): Follow the signs from Mex 1 in Todos Santos. Parking is right on the beach. Other guide pins from this position: surf-forecast San-Pedrito_Todos-Santos 11.4 km.

facts.name: Santo Tomas
facts.windOffshore: NNE (surfnerd wind exposure NNW - ENE, "Offshore from NNE"); N (surfnerd guide text: "north (N) offshore wind")
facts.notes: Surfnerd overview: Santo Tomas is a south-facing right-hand point south of Ensenada, where the highway pulls away from the coast and dirt trails drop down to a cluster of wind-protected breaks. Alongside the main point there's some rocky beachbreak and a rivermouth to explore. The point holds good wind protection, and kelp helps keep the water glassy. Check: surfnerd states facing SSW but best swell W (67.5 degrees apart); both are as published. Skill (surfnerd): Intermediate. Access (surfnerd): Follow the signs for La Bocana / Punta China, and bring a 4WD, which is recommended for the dirt approach. There's camping on hand, along with free roadside parking.

facts.name: Scorpion Bay
facts.windOffshore: W (surfnerd wind exposure SW - NW, "Offshore from W"); NW (surfnerd guide text: "northwest (NW) offshore wind"); West-northwest (surf-forecast)
hazards: Watch for urchins on the boulders. (surfnerd)
facts.notes: Surfnerd overview: Scorpion Bay is a well-documented right-hand point setup at San Juanico, where a swell can peel along any of up to seven righthand points. When it's big enough, those points link together for rides of up to 2 km. The waves break over boulders and sand. Check: surfnerd states facing E but best swell SW (135 degrees apart); both are as published. Skill (surfnerd): Intermediate. Surf-forecast Scorpion-Bay: "Scorpion Bay in Baja Sur is an exposed point break that has fairly inconsistent surf but when it's on it can be World Class. Really long rides are possible. A while back, Surfer Magazine ranked it the 36th best wave in the world while Long Board Mag ranked it in the top ten. Summer offers the best conditions for surfing here. Groundswells are more frequent than windswells and the best swell direction is from the south southwest. Hazards include urchins and rocks." Access (surfnerd): You pay to park and camp on the bluffs above the waves, and there are showers on hand. Getting here is a mission: roughly a 14-hour drive from the US border, with a 4x4 advisable, and there are no services once you arrive. Keep an eye out for scorpions around camp. Other guide pins from this position: surf-forecast Scorpion-Bay 2.7 km.

facts.name: Shipwrecks
facts.windOffshore: NW (surfnerd wind exposure W - N, "Offshore from NW"); NW (surfnerd guide text: "northwest (NW) offshore wind")
facts.notes: Surfnerd overview: Shipwrecks is a punchy right-hand reef break on the desert edge of the Sea of Cortez, out past Costa Azul where the hotels give way to open desert. It's a major landmark among a string of right pointbreaks reached by a wild trail through the desert. The right walls have plenty of punch but rarely barrel, though the adjacent beachbreak left can. Nine Palms, just along the coast, is often a better bet and sits well sheltered from the wind. Skill (surfnerd): Intermediate. Access (surfnerd): There's camping right at the spot and free parking, which is why so many surfers post up here to wait for the swell.

facts.name: Stone Island
facts.swellExposure: SE to SW, SW to WSW (surfnerd)
facts.windOffshore: NNE (surfnerd wind exposure NNW - ENE, "Offshore from NNE"); East-northeast (surf-forecast)
facts.season: Spring, Summer, Autumn (surfnerd); Summer, most often August (surf-forecast)
facts.notes: Surfnerd overview: Stone Island, or Isla de la Piedra, sits just across the harbor from Mazatlan, but its mellow mood and open spaces make it feel much further from the city than a ten-minute ferry ride. You'll find a long stretch of golden beach lined with some of the best open-air restaurants around, and a spread of breaks over sand and rock: A-frame sandbar peaks with rights and lefts, plus the rare right-hand "point" of Escollera. It's a decent, genuinely fun setup, and worth packing for the day rather than a quick session. Skill (surfnerd): Beginner, Intermediate, Expert. Surf-forecast Stone-Islands-Peaks: "Stone Islands Peaks in Sinaloa is an exposed beach break that has reasonably consistent surf and can work at any time of the year. Offshore winds are from the east northeast. Clean groundswells prevail and the best swell direction is from the southwest. The beach break provides left and right handers. When it's working here, it can get crowded. Surfing here means negotiating dangerous rips." Surf-forecast Stone-Islands-Escollera: "Stone Islands Escollera in Sinaloa is an exposed point break that has quite consistent surf. Summer offers the best conditions for surfing. Offshore winds are from the east northeast. Clean groundswells prevail and the best swell direction is from the southwest. It's sometimes crowded here. Hazards include urchins, rocks and pollution." Access (surfnerd): A short ferry ride across the harbor gets you there. Other guide pins from this position: surf-forecast Stone-Islands-Peaks 0.1 km, surf-forecast Stone-Islands-Escollera 1.3 km.

facts.name: The Estuary
facts.windOffshore: NW (surfnerd wind exposure W - N, "Offshore from NW")
facts.tide: Mid (Best at Mid, Better on rising) (surfnerd)
hazards: Bacterial infections are the main hazard, so weigh the water quality before you paddle out. (surfnerd)
facts.notes: Surfnerd overview: The Estuary, also known as La Bocana, is San Jose Del Cabo's city break: a sand-bottom rivermouth on the east side of the town's beachline, tucked into Estero San Jose, a peaceful park that is supposed to be a protected wildlife sanctuary. Being the city break comes at a cost, and the water here is quite polluted. This is one of the most fickle waves in the Cabo area. At its best, which happens maybe once every few years after a big storm washes the coastal berm away, it becomes a perfect A-frame that tubes in both directions. That rare perfection is a double-edged sword, because the same heavy rains flush sewage, animal cadavers, trees, and anything else that floats straight out to the lineup. On average days there are a few scattered peaks around, and those mediocre waves may be less polluted. Skill (surfnerd): Beginner, Intermediate, Expert. Access (surfnerd): Park at La Playita and walk down, or park at El Presidente and walk over.

facts.windOffshore: WNW (surfnerd wind exposure WSW - NNW, "Offshore from WNW"); S (surfnerd guide text: "south (S) offshore wind"); West-northwest (surf-forecast)
hazards: As the tide drops, the rocks and urchins sit closer to the surface, so higher water is both safer and better. (surfnerd)
facts.season: Spring, Summer, Autumn (surfnerd); Summer, most often May (surf-forecast)
facts.notes: Surfnerd overview: The Rock is a challenging right-hand reef break and one of the three sections that make up Costa Azul on Mexico's south shore. It breaks over uneven reef and sand, and the whole lineup is studded with big rocks, so it rewards surfers who can read a shifting, rocky takeoff. The wave itself is genuinely fun and holds size, though a few awkward and occasionally mushy sections can make it tricky to negotiate. Skill (surfnerd): Expert. Surf-forecast The-Rock_Costa-Azul: "The Rock-Costa Azul in Baja Sur is an exposed reef break that has consistent surf. Summer offers the best conditions for surfing. Offshore winds blow from the south. Tends to receive distant groundswells and the ideal swell direction is from the south. A right hand reef break. Likely to be crowded if working. Watch out for urchins, rocks and locals." Access (surfnerd): There's a surf shop on hand, and parking is restricted. Park at Zippers and walk over, or leave the car near Cabo Surf Hotel and walk in. Other guide pins from this position: surf-forecast The-Rock_Costa-Azul 11.8 km.

facts.notes: Surfnerd overview: Todos Santos - La Pastora sits on the Tropic of Cancer, a few miles north of the small village of Todos Santos near the windmills. Winter swells bring big rights, while summer south swells make it peakier. Skill (surfnerd): Beginner.

facts.name: Zipolite
facts.facing: S (surfnerd zipolite-oaxaca: "Faces S"); SSW (surfnerd zipolite: "Faces SSW")
facts.windOffshore: N (surfnerd wind exposure NW - NE, "Offshore from N"); North (surf-forecast)
hazards: The water is typically pretty clean, and sunburn is the main thing to watch out for. (surfnerd)
facts.season: Spring, Summer, Autumn (surfnerd); Winter, most often November (surf-forecast)
facts.notes: Surfnerd overview: Zipolite is a sand-and-rock beachbreak on the wild stretch of coast south of Puerto Escondido, where jungled hills run straight into the Pacific and the beaches stay empty. Along with nearby San Agustinillo, it's a wave for surfers in the mood for something mellow. It's rarely great, and both waves tend to get wind-tattered and warbled after 11am, but it's often fun and worth the paddle. Travelers just passing through probably won't score it. Post up at one of the cheap places for a few hot, quiet days and your odds go up a lot, and there are hidden gems scattered all along this coastline. Surfnerd has 2 entries for this break with different stated facings (zipolite-oaxaca=S, zipolite=SSW); seaward uses the primary entry (zipolite-oaxaca), both kept. Second Surfnerd entry https://www.surfnerd.com/surf-forecast/zipolite: workable swell S - NW (Best from S), 3ft - 8ft, Sand, Beach, Left, Right, Mid, High, Beginner. Skill (surfnerd): Beginner, Intermediate, Expert. Surf-forecast Zipolite: "Zipolite in Oaxaca is an exposed beach break that has quite reliable surf. Summer offers the favoured conditions for surfing. Ideal winds are from the north. Most of the surf here comes from groundswells and the ideal swell angle is from the south southwest. Waves at the beach are both lefts and rights. When the surf is up, it can get quite busy in the water. Hazards include sharks,." Access (surfnerd): Getting to the water is easy. Other guide pins from this position: surf-forecast Zipolite 2.2 km, surfnerd zipolite 1.8 km.

facts.name: Zippers - Costa Azul
facts.windOffshore: WNW (surfnerd wind exposure WSW - NNW, "Offshore from WNW"); NW (surfnerd guide text: "northwest (NW) offshore wind"); Northwest (surf-forecast)
facts.tide: Low, Mid, High (surfnerd); Good surf at all stages of the tide. (surf-forecast)
hazards: urchins, rips, rocks, locals and pollution (surf-forecast)
facts.season: Spring, Summer, Autumn (surfnerd); Summer, most often May (surf-forecast)
facts.notes: Surfnerd overview: Zippers is a river mouth right in the Cabo San Lucas region, and one of the best waves around. It peaks up gently outside a patch of exposed rocks, giving a smooth, easy takeoff, then runs almost laterally along a cobblestone reef, gathering speed as it heads into an inside section full of hackable lips and air sections. The wave holds its size all the way down the line, so you can keep stacking turns on a single ride. A few good ones here can make the whole session. Skill (surfnerd): Expert. Surf-forecast Zippers_Costa-Azul: "Zippers-Costa Azul in Baja Sur is an exposed beach and reef break that has consistent surf. Summer offers the optimum conditions for surfing. Offshore winds are from the northwest. Clean groundswells prevail and the best swell direction is from the south. A right hand reef break. Good surf at all stages of the tide. A popular wave that can get growded. Beware of urchins, rips, rocks, locals and pollution." Access (surfnerd): There's a surf shop nearby, and parking is restricted. Other guide pins from this position: surf-forecast Zippers_Costa-Azul 11.9 km.
